feature: in-DB cross-chain bridge linking (2a) - generation 2 (hardened after boundary review)
hardening: Bidirectional isolated 1:1 matching (OUT has one eligible IN AND that IN has one eligible OUT); greedy forward-only claimedInIds removed.
Self-healing: candidacy re-derived every run (no bridge_group_id skip), idempotent no-op write skip, per-pair try/catch; a mid-pair write failure is repaired on the next run.
Canonical asset identity (native / canonical WETH / canonical USDC+USDT contracts) instead of symbol-only; an unknown or spoofed same-symbol token never links.
Provider-path coverage: an OUT to a LI.FI / Across / Stargate registry address emits bridge_suspected.

commands.summary: 13 files; 142 tests (bridge-linking 11 incl. hardening cases; provider-path adapter test; coexisting historical-price work).

endToEnd.evidence: After reset+resync (208 rows, 0 skips): USDT bridge 0xee478fda linked via canonical contracts (OUT 0xc2132d05 Polygon USDT + IN 0xdac17f958 Ethereum USDT) both INTERNAL_TRANSFER, dest=1, destination rescued from SPAM. ETH bridge 0x798d722 native<->native linked, dest=10. Third OUT 0xf1a2870 (no candidate) stays SEND flagged. Canonical-asset hardening still links the real bridges while a spoof would not.
